channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: New Emergence Art Prize 2026
item.description: An international online art prize for emerging artists working in any medium, including photography, founded by artist Habib Hajallie RBA. With a prize fund of over £5,000, the 2026 edition awards a £1,000 grand prize alongside a two-week NG Art Creative Residency in Provence, France, a year on Parker Harris's Art Ladder mentoring programme, and several materials awards. The judging panel includes Addi Aegisdottir, Creative Director of the Mall Galleries. Open to artists worldwide with no set theme; up to three works may be submitted and selected work is presented online. Deadline 3 August 2026. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: £15–£30. Prize: £1,000 + Residency + Mentoring.

item.title: Call for Proposals for Solo Exhibitions · CSU Spur
item.description: CSU Spur, the Colorado State University System's public-facing campus at Denver's National Western Center, invites solo exhibition proposals for 2026–2027 celebrating the intersection of community, sustainability and innovation. Work exploring environmental stewardship, scientific curiosity and local storytelling is sought, with proposals around food, water and health especially encouraged. Open to artists of all experience levels working in any medium including photography; the galleries are public campus spaces. Submissions are reviewed quarterly on a rolling basis until the call closes November 1, 2026, with exhibition dates set in collaboration with campus staff. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Solo/Group Show 2027 · Gallery 40
item.description: Gallery 40, the contemporary gallery at 40 Cannon Street in Poughkeepsie, is selecting artists for its 2027 solo and small-group exhibition program. Chosen artists — solo or in curated groups of up to four — receive a six-week show from February 6 to March 14, 2027 with an opening reception, and may be considered for artist talks, panel discussions or recorded interviews. All 2-dimensional work is considered, explicitly including photography; work must be for sale (40% commission), no larger than 48 x 48 inches framed, ready to hang, and not previously exhibited at the gallery. Open to US artists 18 and over; submissions are evaluated by the gallery's curators. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 10 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: IN SERIES · Art Fluent
item.description: Art Fluent's open call for a cohesive body of work — five pieces built around a single idea, shown as a mini solo show within a larger online group exhibition. Open to all fine art media including photography, worldwide, amateur and professional. Each accepted artist receives a $250 cash prize and a place in the online gallery at art-fluent.com. Curated by Creative Director Amy Matteson Neill and an anonymous committee; deadline October 9, 2026 (midnight MST), notification November 6. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $35 for a series of 5. Prize: $250 per accepted artist.

item.title: Photography+ Open Call: Un/Stable — Lands, Anxieties, Dreams · Photoworks
item.description: Open call for the next issue of Photography+, Photoworks' online magazine, on the theme 'Un/Stable: Lands, Anxieties, Dreams' — work responding to the fragile, shifting conditions shaping our lives, environments, and collective futures, from displacement and ecological change to anxiety, resilience, care, and adaptation, and how photography can hold space for possibility. Submit a single image responding to the theme; one selected work receives an £80 artist fee and is featured in the upcoming issue of Photography+. Open to anyone, anywhere in the world, with no professional experience required. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £80 + Publication.

item.title: (S)Light of Hand 2026 · The Photographer's Eye Collective
item.description: The Photographer's Eye Collective's annual juried celebration of alternative, historical, and experimental photographic processes, staged at its nonprofit gallery on Grand Avenue in Escondido, California. Handmade, photo-based work is welcome — from albumen and cyanotype to ziatype, plus hand-worked digital or silver prints incorporating collage, stitching, or three-dimensional elements. The 2026 edition is juried by Ann M. Jastrab, Executive Director of the Center for Photographic Art in Carmel, with Juror's Choice and Director's Choice honors receiving an online exhibition and a printed catalog in 2027. Selected works are shown in the gallery 12 September – 31 October 2026, opening with a reception on 12 September. Open to photographers 18 and older; up to ten images per artist. — Deadline: August 7, 2026. Fee: $35 for 5 images; $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Animals 2026 · Grid Photo Gallery
item.description: International call from Grid Photo Gallery for work that engages with animal life in its many forms — wildlife, documentary, portraiture, fine art, conceptual, studio, and experimental photography are all welcome. Selection favours visual clarity, sensitivity of approach, and a strong awareness of form rather than any single genre. Selected work is shown in a curated online exhibition on the gallery site. First place is named Photographer of the Month with a profile interview, priority promotional placement, and a free entry in the next open call; second and third places are highlighted in the virtual exhibition. All selected entries receive permanent online display, social media promotion, a digital certificate, and a profile page linking to the photographer's site. The exhibition opens 1 September 2026. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: €7. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Head On Photo Awards 2026
item.description: The flagship international awards of Sydney's Head On Photo Festival, judged completely anonymously — jurors see the photograph, never the photographer's name, CV or following. Three categories: Portrait, Landscape and Exposure (anything that is not portrait or landscape), sharing an AUD 80,000 prize pool that includes AUD 5,000 cash for each category winner plus OM System camera kits. Around 40 finalists per category (20–30 for Exposure) are exhibited in print and online during the festival, 6–29 November 2026. Open internationally to photographers at every level, from phone snapshots to studio and documentary work. Entries are AUD 30 per image, half price for under-25s; final deadline 16 August 2026, 11:59pm Sydney time. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $30 AUD per image; under-25s $15. Prize: AUD 80,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Prix LNP 2026 — Les Nuits Photo
item.description: The annual call for photographic films from Les Nuits Photo, the Paris festival devoted to the photo-film form, organised by the photographers' association Freelens in partnership with SAIF. Open internationally to all authors — established, emerging, students and amateurs alike, whether photographers, directors, editors, artists or journalists. The Grand Prix LNP carries a €1,000 award from SAIF plus diffusion on Fisheye Magazine and 9 Lives Magazine and screenings at partner festivals; the Prix LNP Diapéro, chosen by the Diapéro team, adds €500 and paid distribution on Mediapart. Submissions run 20 June – 15 September 2026 via Google Form; prizes are presented at the festival in Paris in November. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,000 + Publication.

item.title: Bourse Transverse 2026 · Freelens / ADAGP
item.description: Joint grant from photographers' association Freelens and ADAGP, the French visual-arts authors' society, supporting a duo — a photographer and an artist from another visual discipline — in creating a work together and publishing it as a book. €12,000 in total: €7,000 to the winning duo and €5,000 towards the book's edition, with the work made within a year and the book published within two. Open to duos from the French scene (working or residing in France for at least five years, or French nationals living abroad) with professional track records of exhibitions or publications; a publisher may already be attached. Applications in French via the ADAGP candidature portal by 3 September 2026, 2pm; the winning duo is announced at Salon Polycopies in Paris on 12 November 2026. — Deadline: September 3, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €7,000 + Publication.

item.title: ABSURIA — International Abstract & Surrealist Photography Contest 2027
item.description: Second edition of the international festival dedicated exclusively to abstract and surrealist photography. Open to amateur and professional photographers worldwide. 100 photographs selected for physical exhibition across multiple venues in Tours, Loire Valley, France from May to September 2027, with all nominees also shown in 3D online galleries on the festival website. Fourteen winners honoured at the awards ceremony in Tours in early May 2027. Categories: Abstract Photography and Surrealist Photography, each with Professional and Amateur divisions plus a Young Hopefuls award; winners receive the ABSURIA Trophy, a gold statuette created for the contest. Fee tiered by number of works: amateur €20–€40, professional €25–€50, up to 6 works per registration with unlimited registrations. Images created solely with generative AI are excluded. — Deadline: April 30, 2027. Fee: €20–€50. Prize: Exhibition + trophy.

item.title: Booooooom x Format Creative Development Program
item.description: A free mentorship and portfolio development program from art platform Booooooom and portfolio-builder Format, aimed at visual artists, illustrators and photographers who are ready to grow rather than those with the most polished work. The grand prize recipient receives a lifetime Format subscription, personal mentorship with Booooooom editor-in-chief Jeff Hamada, and featured coverage on both platforms; two runners-up each receive a one-year Format plan and a portfolio review with Format's Stanzie Tooth. To apply, sign up for a free 60-day Format trial (no credit card required), build a portfolio of original work, and submit two short written statements — one describing the work, one on where you are in your practice and what support you're looking for. Open worldwide to artists 18+. Applications close September 2, 2026, 11:59pm PT. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Mentorship + Format subscription.

item.title: BWP x Nikon Grant Fund 2026 — Quarter 3 · Black Women Photographers
item.description: Third-quarter 2026 cycle of the Black Women Photographers x Nikon $50K Grant Fund — a year-long program supporting Black women photographers globally through four quarterly grant opportunities. The Q3 recipient receives a $2,500 USD unrestricted cash grant plus a Nikon Z6III with 24-70mm f/4 lens kit. Funding can support photography projects, production, travel, equipment, or other professional needs. BWP is a global membership community founded in 2020 by Polly Irungu, with members across 60+ countries and 35 U.S. states. Applications for Q3 close August 16, 2026; a final Q4 cycle follows later in the year. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $2,500 + Nikon Z6III kit.

item.title: Outdoor Photography Magazine — Summer Woodland
item.description: Submit up to 5 summer woodland images with captions for the 'One Thing This Month' feature (OP 332) in Outdoor Photography Magazine (UK). Winner receives a Vanguard VEO 3 303AB aluminium tripod (RRP £250). Captions up to 75 words with technical details (camera, lens, focal length, ISO, shutter speed, aperture). Entries upload via Google Form. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Vanguard tripod (£250) + Publication.

item.title: Photobook Dummy Exhibition — 16th Lisbon Photobook Fair
item.description: Open call for the photobook dummy exhibition of the 16th Feira do Livro de Fotografia de Lisboa, held November 27–29, 2026 at the Arquivo Municipal de Lisboa – Fotográfico. Dummies are displayed for consultation throughout the fair, where past editions (72 projects by 65 authors in 2026) have drawn the attention of attending publishers and booksellers — a real chance to move a book project forward. Pre-register with up to 6 photographs of the dummy (72 dpi, max 2 MB each) via the Google Form by October 12, 21:00 GMT; confirmations October 23, dummies delivered by November 16. Participation is free. The fair also runs parallel calls for self-publisher/small-press tables and presentations of authorial projects. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Small Works on Paper 2027 · Arkansas Arts Council
item.description: Annual juried exhibition of the Arkansas Arts Council, touring up to ten venues across the state for a full year starting January 2027 at the South Arkansas Arts Center in El Dorado. Open to Arkansas residents 18+ working on paper — painting, photography, drawing, printmaking, mixed media and collage; work must be from the past two years and fit an 18×18 or 18×24 inch frame; no AI. Juror Kathy Liao (Joan Mitchell Foundation Fellow, 21c Artadia awardee) selects a maximum of 40 works, with up to $2,000 available in purchase awards for the SWOP permanent collection. Selected artists join the council's Juried Artist Directory. Entries July 15 – August 23, 2026 via CaFÉ. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $15 for 1, $25 for 3. Prize: $2,000 purchase awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Artist in Residence Program — Palm Springs Preferred Small Hotels
item.description: Inaugural juried photography residency from the Palm Springs boutique-hotel collective, creating the first coordinated visual archive of the city's small-hotel legacy. Up to 12 photographers are hosted for 1–2 weeks across roughly 18 properties in three sessions (November 8–21 and December 6–19, 2026; January 18–30, 2027), receiving complimentary lodging, a $250 weekly stipend, transportation support, attraction passes and mentorship from photographer Terry Hastings. Architectural, documentary, fine art, experimental, multimedia and AI-assisted practices welcome; the first call focuses on Southern California photographers. The season concludes with a curated exhibition and sales showcase at the Palm Springs Cultural Center. Apply with 3–10 images via CaFÉ. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Residency + $250/week stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Art That Matters to the Planet: Dark Skies · Roger Tory Peterson Institute
item.description: Sixth annual juried exhibition at the Roger Tory Peterson Institute in Jamestown, NY (January 29 – May 30, 2027), themed on the night skies after Peterson's A Field Guide to the Stars and Planets — nocturnal creatures, constellations, light pollution and space junk. All media welcome, including photography; recent works (since 2020) preferred. Guest juror Jon Lomberg, Carl Sagan's principal artistic collaborator and Design Director of NASA's Voyager Golden Record. For the first time RTPI awards cash prizes of $1,000, $500 and $250, announced at the opening reception. International; up to 4 works. Entries open August 1 and close November 7, 2026 via CaFÉ. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $20 + $10/extra work. Prize: $1,000 / $500 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: Tracks & Trails: Marks Left Behind · View Arts Center
item.description: Winter juried exhibition in the largest galleries of View Arts Center in Old Forge, NY, in the Adirondacks (December 11, 2026 – March 6, 2027). The theme investigates stories written upon the land — animal tracks, footprints, ski and snowshoe trails, railroads, bridges and winter logging — the marks that become part of the landscape's memory. All media welcome, including photography. Open to US artists; work must be original, created within the past 3 years and not previously shown at View. Up to 3 works ($35 first, $10 each additional) via CaFÉ; artists receive 65% of sales. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: $35 + $10/extra work. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Künstler*dorf Schöppingen Residency Fellowships 2027
item.description: Around 40 residency fellowships per year at the artists' village in Schöppingen, North Rhine-Westphalia, for professional visual artists (including photographers), authors and composers. Residencies of 2–6 months during 2027, with a stipend of €1,500 per month (minus roughly €100–200 for rent and operating costs); collectives receive €1,000 per person up to €3,000. Open to all nationalities and ages; partners, family or assistance can be accommodated by arrangement. Not a production fellowship — no obligation to present results, though exhibition and presentation facilities are available. Expert juries select on quality of previous work, the Schöppingen project and community contributions. Apply June 27 – August 31, 2026 via the online portal. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Residency + €1,500/month stipend.

item.title: Queer Spirit · Blackfish Gallery
item.description: Open call from Blackfish Gallery, the artist-run cooperative gallery founded in 1979 in Portland's Pearl District, for Queer Spirit, a group exhibition running January 6–30, 2027. The gallery invites greater Portland-based artists whose work engages with queer identity, community, and imagination — across all backgrounds — for a celebration of resilience, belonging, and radical imagination. Submissions may directly address queer identity, explore the broader possibilities of queerness, or reflect the perspectives of queer artists; work across all media is welcome, with particular interest in experimental, thought-provoking, and installation-based practices. Free to enter via EntryThingy. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Cantua Editions Open Call for Submissions
item.description: Annual submissions call from Cantua Editions, an independent artist-run publishing house in New Jersey producing limited-edition hand-bound photobooks and ephemera, with publications held by MIT's Rotch Library and Harvard's Fine Arts Library. Seeking primarily photo-based projects exploring how landscapes, environments, and communities shape one another; artists working with archives and historical documentation are also welcome, as are themes of memory, ecology, and preservation. Send a short artist bio, a project statement (max 500 words), and 20–30 images as a single PDF to books.cantuaeditions@gmail.com with the subject line 'Submission – [Your Name]'. Chosen artists are invited to a preliminary meeting toward a publication. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: UNSTAGED — How Are Things?
item.description: Open call from UNSTAGED, the independent photography journal of narrative-led inquiries into comforting and discomforting authenticity, initiated with the How Are Things Collective founded by Professor Amanda Crawley Jackson (University of the Arts London). The call explores how creative practice — photography in particular — can hold space for urgent dialogue and reflection in a time of polycrisis: projects examining our entanglement with human, non-human and more-than-human entities, bodies, and structures, through material & affective, political & (infra)structural, or speculative lenses. Submit 5–10 photographs as JPGs (long edge 2000px, 300 DPI) with a project description (max 500 words) via a public Google Drive link emailed to opencall@un-staged.com — email attachments are not considered. Free entry with no contribution fee; selected work is curated for print. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Salon — London Photo Show November 2026
item.description: Open call for The Salon, a juried group exhibition at Hoxton Arches in London, November 26–29, 2026. Selected images are professionally printed (10×8 inches with a white border) and displayed with the photographer's name in the gallery. Open to photographers at all experience levels, whether or not they have exhibited before. Standout entries receive partner prizes from Think Tank, 36exp and Point 101, including a large-format archival Hahnemühle print and future exhibition space. Submit 1, 3 or 5 images (£35 / £90 / £125) via the entry form; upload instructions follow by email. — Deadline: November 19, 2026. Fee: £35–£125. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Annual Exhibition 2027 — Royal Scottish Academy Building · Visual Arts Scotland
item.description: Visual Arts Scotland's flagship annual open exhibition returns to the Upper Galleries of the Royal Scottish Academy Building on Princes Street, Edinburgh, in January 2027, in partnership with ESSA. Open globally to members and non-members across all visual arts and contemporary craft, including fine-art photography. Submit up to 5 works completed within the last three years and not previously shown at the RSA or with VAS in the past five years. Non-members pay £15 per work; VAS members submit their first three works free. Selected artists pay a one-time £15 installation fee, and sales carry a 40% commission (35% for Professional Members). Selection results announced September 17, 2026. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: £15 per work (members free). Prize: None listed.

item.title: DEAR DAVE, Fellowships 2026
item.description: Annual fellowship competition from DEAR DAVE, the New York tri-annual print magazine of photography and writing published since 2007. Open to photographers worldwide with no limitation of genre or topic — submit a cohesive body of work of 10 to 20 images. Three selected photographers have their portfolios featured in an upcoming issue of the magazine, and the 40 highest-ranked entrants join the Fellowship Archive on the magazine's website. The jury spans curators, editors and gallerists including Peter Barberie (Philadelphia Museum of Art), Tim Clark (1000 Words), Kristen Lubben (Magnum Foundation) and Domenico de Chirico (Unseen Photo). Previous publication or exhibition does not disqualify applicants. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $18. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Quiet Hours: Nighttime and Grief · Der Greif
item.description: Open call from Der Greif inviting lens-based artists to examine nighttime's emotional landscape — how darkness changes the way we see the world and how we feel. Timed around National Grief Awareness Day, the call centres on grief in its many manifestations: bereavement, relationship loss, displacement, or life transitions, and asks how darkness and light can convey narratives of memory and healing. Selected work is featured in an online exhibition on Der Greif's Pulse platform, with facilitated peer critique sessions and exposure within Der Greif's international network, plus potential invitations to submit portfolios for sales and commission opportunities. Entry is free with an optional €5–€10 donation, and 50–100% discount vouchers are available for artists facing financial barriers. — Deadline: August 8, 2026. Fee: Free (optional €5–€10 donation). Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Group Show II — Guest Curator Jesse Lenz · Hypam Editions
item.description: Second group show from Hypam Editions, the Louisville, Kentucky photo curatorial project, hosted at Misc. Goods Co., Hypam's home base. Guest curated by Jesse Lenz — photographer, founder and director of Charcoal Book Club, Charcoal Press, and the Chico Hot Springs Portfolio Review. No theme: submit up to 10 images that best represent your photographic practice or a cohesive body of work; emerging and established photographers both encouraged. Selected artists print, frame and ship their work (max 36 inches on the long side). Acceptance notification September 4; the show opens October 17 with a reception featuring a Charcoal Press/Book Club booth. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Apeldoorn Photo Award 2026 — Sporen (Traces)
item.description: First edition of the Apeldoorn Photo Award, a new biennial photo competition organised by the Dutch photography platform Apeldoorn Photo with the Municipality of Apeldoorn. Theme "Sporen" (Traces) — what people, time and nature leave behind — across three categories: Nature in Motion, Human Traces, and Silent Witnesses. Open to photographers from the Netherlands and abroad; submit up to 3 photos in one category via the Pixoroo platform. Category winners each receive €500, and the audience-prize winner receives €500 plus a solo exhibition at the 2027 Apeldoorn Photo Festival. Longlisted works are exhibited in central Apeldoorn with public voting; exhibiting artists pay a €150 contribution covering print production and the award catalogue. Jury chaired by photographer Maarten Corbijn. Award ceremony November 25, 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: €15 (€150 if selected). Prize: €500 per category + Solo exhibition.

item.title: .ART Award 2026
item.description: Inaugural global award marking the 10th anniversary of the .ART domain registry, open to artists worldwide across all disciplines including photography and lens-based work. A single overarching prize combines a $15,000 cash Grand Prize, one-month residencies at Château du Fresne near Paris and Anfitrion in Marbella, Spain (both with round-trip travel), editorial coverage in international art media, and a premium .ART domain valued at $10,000. Jury includes critic Jerry Saltz alongside curators and gallerists. Free to enter, but applicants must register and link a .ART domain to their portfolio; multiple entries are allowed, each needing its own domain. Submit an artist biography, artwork documentation, and a short narrative explaining the concept. Winners announced December 3, 2026 during Art Basel Miami. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free (needs .ART domain). Prize: $15,000 + Residencies + Publication.

item.title: Paper Photo Dummy Award 2026 · Paper Photo Festival
item.description: The dummies & zines category of the Paper Photo Festival in Sosnowiec, Poland — dedicated to photobooks in book form rather than the individual photographs. Open to unpublished photobook dummies (paper form) created after 1 January 2025, as well as self-published works and zines with a print run of no more than 30 copies. Judging focuses on how the artistic idea resonates as a book object. The main prize is PLN 5,000 (around €1,150), with individual honours from jury members. Six shortlisted authors are invited to Sosnowiec with accommodation during the opening weekend, and roughly 30 dummies are exhibited at the festival, 18–20 September 2026. Enter via the online form and mail a copy of the dummy (delivery date decisive) by 18 August 2026; shortlist announced by 1 September. — Deadline: August 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: PLN 5,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Eyeshot Open Call 2026
item.description: The annual open call from Eyeshot, the Italy-based street and documentary photography publisher, framed as 'a reading' rather than a contest. Singles (1–15 photographs) compete for cash prizes of €1,000, €500 and €250, while series of 9, 12 or 15 photographs are considered for a fully funded monograph editorial contract described as a €20,000+ investment; all finalists are published in the Open Call book. Open to everyone, everywhere, with entry fees scaled by country income band and free entry for students and those facing economic hardship. Jury: Newsha Tavakolian (Magnum Photos), Bill Shapiro (formerly LIFE), Matt Stuart, Shin Noguchi and Tavepong Pratoomwong (UP Photographers), with Eyeshot editors Marco Savarese and Lucrezia Bonarota. Submissions 3 July – 6 September 2026; winners announced 9 October 2026. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: €6–€60 by image count & country; students free. Prize: €1,000 + Publication.

item.title: Paper Photo Award 2026 · Paper Photo Festival
item.description: The photobook competition of the Paper Photo Festival in Sosnowiec, Poland. Open to photobooks published in paper form between 1 January 2025 and 30 June 2026, whether self-published or from a publisher, with a minimum print run of 30 copies and photography as the primary medium. The main prize is PLN 10,000 (around €2,300), with additional individual honours from jury members. Six shortlisted authors are invited to Sosnowiec with accommodation, and roughly 30 photobooks are exhibited during the festival, 18–20 September 2026. Enter via the online form and mail a copy of the book (delivery date decisive) by 18 August 2026; shortlist announced by 1 September. — Deadline: August 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: PLN 10,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: World Culture: Art at The Ferguson Library · Stamford Art Association
item.description: Multimedia juried exhibition from the Stamford Art Association on the theme of world culture — food, regional clothing and customs, ceremonies, cultural patterns and abstractions, open to interpretation by artists of all backgrounds and experience levels. Photography, painting, drawing, printmaking and any medium welcome; up to 5 works. Up to $400 in awards for excellence and conformity to the theme, with a 30% commission on sales. Work must be wired for hanging and hand delivered. Shown at The Ferguson Library, 3rd floor, Stamford, September 10, 2026 – January 7, 2027, with an opening reception September 10. — Deadline: August 13, 2026. Fee: $35 + $15 each addl ($30/$10 members). Prize: Up to $400 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: PhotoMonth 2026 Open Call — Unity and Community
item.description: PhotoMonth, East London's international photography festival (founded in 2001, relaunched in 2025), returns in October 2026 with an open-call group exhibition on the theme 'Unity and Community' — reflecting, questioning and celebrating the relationships that shape communities, identities and collective experience amid a drift toward division and discrimination. Open to all photographers and lens-based artists worldwide, regardless of age or career level, in any photographic style or medium, with experimental and expanded forms encouraged. Free to submit up to 3 images; selected artists pay a £20 participation fee (£12 concessions). Selected work is shown at The Art Pavilion, Mile End Park, London, 15–25 October 2026, with an opening celebration on 14 October. Curated by Cherelle Sappleton, Tom Hunter, Ishy Pryce-Parchment and Leah Mclaine. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free entry; £20 if selected (£12 concessions). Prize: None listed.

item.title: Create! Magazine Tenth Anniversary Art Prize 2026
item.description: Create! Magazine's flagship annual juried art prize, marking the publication's tenth anniversary. Open worldwide across four categories — Photography and Digital Art (film, digital photography and new media, AI excluded), Painting and Two-Dimensional Media, Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Design, and Fiber and Textile Art. The grand-prize winner receives $1,000, a six-page editorial spread and interview in the print magazine, a podcast guest appearance, a spot in the Philadelphia pop-up exhibition (October 2026) and a social feature to an audience of 200,000+. First-place winners in each category receive a one-year Create! Collective membership ($390 value), a two-page feature, exhibition participation and a blog interview. Enter three images for $35; a limited number of fee-waiver scholarships are available on request. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 / 3 images. Prize: $1,000 + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: Crocker Kingsley 2027 · Blue Line Arts
item.description: A long-running national juried competition presented by Blue Line Arts in Roseville, California, open to all media including photography. Juried by Naz Cuguoğlu, curator of contemporary art at the Asian Art Museum in San Francisco. Selected works are shown across Blue Line Arts' four galleries (January 2–February 13, 2027), and a selection travels to the Crocker Art Museum in Sacramento. Cash awards total $5,500 across five places. Open to US residents 18 and over; original work completed in the last two years that has not previously been exhibited at Blue Line Arts. Entry is $45 for the first image plus $5 for each additional image (up to 10 more). — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $45 + $5/additional image. Prize: $2,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: VMFA Visual Arts Fellowship 2027–28
item.description: The Virginia Museum of Fine Arts' long-standing fellowship program supporting Virginia's visual artists and art students, having awarded more than $6.5 million to date. Photography is an explicit eligible discipline (alongside crafts, drawing, film/video, mixed media, new/emerging media, painting, printmaking, sculpture and art history). Fellowships are $8,000 for professional individual/collaborative artists, $6,000 for graduate students and $4,000 for undergraduates, funding work during the May 2027–May 2028 period. No application fee. Open to US citizens or permanent residents who have been legal residents of Virginia for at least 24 consecutive months before the deadline; professional artists and full-time graduate/undergraduate students. Submit eight digital work samples. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $4,000–$8,000 Fellowship.

item.title: Weather Photographer of the Year 2026 · Royal Meteorological Society
item.description: The Royal Meteorological Society's long-running global competition celebrating photography that captures the power, beauty and impact of weather, now in its second decade. Open to photographers of all levels worldwide, it recognises both dramatic weather events and the growing influence of climate change. Categories: Weather Photographer of the Year (£1,500), Mobile Weather Photographer of the Year for images shot on a smartphone or tablet (£500), the Climate Award for work telling a compelling story about our changing climate (£500), and a Public Favourite decided by global online vote. Free to enter. Shortlist and public vote late October; winners announced 17 November 2026. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,500.

item.title: Composed · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont, in collaboration with the Texas Photographic Society, celebrating the art of photographic composition — work where framing, perspective, light, color, geometry and visual organization are fundamental to the image's impact. Juried by documentary photographer Brian Finke, whose work on the authenticity and absurdity of everyday life has appeared in National Geographic, The New York Times and The New Yorker. Up to 35 images are selected for the gallery exhibition and about 40 more for the online gallery, all appearing in the exhibition catalog and remaining on the gallery website. Open to photographers worldwide; enter up to 12 images. Exhibition runs October 2–31, 2026, with prints due September 18. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: $40 ($30 members) / 5 images + $5 each. Prize: $500 / $300 / $100 + Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Through the Looking Glass · WHAM Art Association
item.description: WHAM Art Center in Surprise, Arizona invites artists to explore perspective in all its forms — literal, emotional, symbolic and imagined — engaging perception, reflection, transformation and imagination. All media welcome, including photography; work may be literal, abstract, symbolic or conceptual. Entry is $40 for up to five works (a related series counts as one); all pieces must be original, gallery-ready and priced for sale. Open to artists of all levels aged 18 and over residing in the United States. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Haus-a-rest — Issue 74: Eco Materials
item.description: UK-based independent art zine seeking visual art (photography, painting, sculpture, ceramics, textiles, video, collage, digital media) and writing (poetry, prose, essays) on the theme 'Eco Materials' — how materials carry histories of extraction, labour, place, memory and transformation, and how making can be an act of care. Edited by Jenna Fox and Nichola Rodgers. Free to submit, open globally, no monetary prize. Selected works are published online and promoted through the zine's Instagram gallery (@haus_a_rest). Issue 74 launches mid-September 2026. Instagram handle is required for submission. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Travel Photographer of the Year 2026
item.description: Long-running international travel photography award, founded in 2003 and judged by a panel of professional photographers and editors. Enter four-image portfolios across Adventures & Journeys, Cultures Traditions & Celebrations, Landscapes (Natural & Urban) and Wildlife/Sealife/Birdlife, or single frames in the One Shot categories: In Nature, People of the World, Street, and Travel in Black & White. Free Young Travel Photographer categories for under-18s and a Rising Talent Award round out the programme. Winners share cash prizes, imaging software and extensive media exposure, with the overall Travel Photographer of the Year title as the headline honour. Early-bird pricing runs to mid-July; entries close October 12 and winners are announced January 17, 2027. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: £14–£99. Prize: Cash awards.

item.title: HOME: States of Belonging · Arvada Center for the Arts and Humanities
item.description: Juried Main Gallery exhibition of contemporary photo-based work at the Arvada Center (January 14 – March 28, 2027), presented in partnership with the Colorado Photographic Arts Center and Denver's Month of Photography. The show explores home as something shaped by identity, memory, movement, family, work and community, and welcomes photography, video, collage, installation, archival and alternative image-making processes. Open to Colorado residents 18+; entries accepted July 17 – October 12, 2026 via CaFÉ, with fee scholarships available for BIPOC and LGBTQIA+ artists and those experiencing hardship. Jurors: Samantha Johnston (CPAC) and Collin Parson (Arvada Center). Artists receive 60% of sales. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: $35 for 3 works. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Hyperview · Manifest Gallery
item.description: An international call for works about vastness and scale at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, open to all traditional and non-traditional genres and media. Selected works are exhibited November 6 – December 4, 2026, in the gallery's 23rd season. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, one work from each exhibition period wins the $1,000 Grand Jury Award, and artists receive 70% on sales. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional entry; open internationally. Notifications by September 28. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Counterform · Manifest Gallery
item.description: A call for works about reactions — the aftermath of change — at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati, open internationally to all traditional and non-traditional genres and media. Selected works are exhibited November 6 – December 4, 2026, alongside Hyperview and Visage in the gallery's 23rd season. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, one work from each exhibition period wins the $1,000 Grand Jury Award, and artists receive 70% on sales. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional entry. Notifications by September 28. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Visage · Manifest Gallery
item.description: An international call for works of portraiture at Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati — traditional and non-traditional approaches in any media, self-portraits or portraits of others, singular figures or groups, from the most traditional to the most conceptual or experimental. Selected works are exhibited November 6 – December 4, 2026, in the gallery's 23rd season. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, one work from each exhibition period wins the $1,000 Grand Jury Award, and artists receive 70% on sales. Submit up to 3 entries for $45, $5 per additional entry. Notifications by September 28. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Wacken Rock 'n Roll Photography Workshop 2026 · Pep Bonet
item.description: Open call for six free places in the 5th Rock 'n Roll Photography Workshop, led by NOOR photojournalist and former Motörhead photographer Pep Bonet with LOUD>SOCIETY during Wacken Open Air 2026 (July 29 – August 1), the world's largest heavy metal festival. Under the anniversary theme 'HARDER', the group shoots, edits and post-produces festival photography on the spot for official W:O:A channels. Selected photographers receive free tuition, on-site hosting, festival ticket, crew catering, all necessary passes and permits, and a shuttle from Hamburg; travel to Hamburg is not covered. Apply with a short bio, motivation letter and portfolio; fluent English required. — Deadline: July 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Workshop fellowship.

item.title: Kominek Editions I — Golden Hour / Blue Hour
item.description: Kominek Gallery — the Berlin gallery and photobook publisher behind books with Alec Soth, Rinko Kawauchi and Viviane Sassen — invites submissions for Kominek Editions I, a group exhibition built on the concept of 100 photographers, 100 images, on the theme Golden Hour / Blue Hour. Email 1–5 images for consideration to info@kominek-gallery.com. Selected photographers are announced August 10; the exhibition opens at the gallery on September 10, 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: FLARE Journal Vol. 2 — Connection X Isolation
item.description: Call for the second print edition of FLARE, a nonprofit journal dedicated to photography of the climate crisis. The Autumn 2026 edition asks for work on the theme Connection X Isolation — how we connect with each other and the non-human world in times of ecological crisis, and how the crisis ruptures connection and creates isolation. Submit individual images or a series of up to 10 (TIFF, minimum 4000 px on the shortest side). A $5–10 donation per submission supports printing and distribution but is optional — all submissions are considered regardless. Contributors retain full copyright. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $5–10 voluntary. Prize: Print publication.
